verdict.rationale: Terraform's docs say anyone can publish and consume modules on the public Terraform Registry. Publishers sign in with a GitHub account, and users can search and filter the registry. Modules are a first-class reuse mechanism, and the community complaint about public-module quality is a quality concern rather than a contradiction of the capability. Missing for 10: detailed documentation of the module source/versioning syntax for consuming registry modules, step-by-step publishing workflow details (e.g., repo naming and release tagging), and hands-on corroboration of publishing.

support.subject: As a developer, I can consume and publish reusable modules or components from a public registry

citations.quote: Anyone can publish and consume providers, modules, and policies on the public Terraform Registry.
Individuals interested in publishing can use a GitHub account to sign in to the Terraform Registry.
Select a provider or module card to learn more, filter results to a specific tier, or use the search field at the top of the Registry.
